body:
Redline round 1

Reviewed the whole pull request.

The coverage pass over the whole pull request at 5a9c2f1 returned 13 candidates: 12 verified, 0 could not be confirmed, 0 refuted, 0 collapsed into items already reported or settled, 1 already tracked.

This pull request moves the question of what a deferral ships from the words of its mitigation to the round's own record, and takes deferrals out of the commit demand. The phrase list is gone, and the wording #100 pins no longer stops a round. The correctness findings are where a decided finding meets the new rules: a fix the person or autopilot decided can drop out of needCommits, through a reshape's re-sort (R1-10) or a stray filled entry beside an override (R1-11), and the plan approver's file-list rule reads the shaper's files where the workflow reads the resolve agent's (R1-2). The rest are a stop view that can go stale, docs and comments that say slightly more than the code does, and code this change left dead. There is no scheduled or queued work in this repository (no routes/console.php). The version moves to 0.4.1 as a patch, and the plan has a Docs entry for every touched file.

### Correctness (4)

- **R1-2** · correctness · medium · confirmed · `agents/redline-plan-approver.md:16` · The approver's file-list bounce reads the shaper's files for a finding the person decided
- **R1-9** · correctness · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:3644` · A draft's version ignores the `ships` and `files` the stop now shows, so an answered draft is not raised again when they change
- **R1-10** · correctness · medium · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:3949` · deferralIds counts a decided call that a reshape re-sorted to defer, so its planned fix is no longer demanded
- **R1-11** · correctness · medium · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:3951` · A person's override to fix is no longer demanded when the resolve agent returns a filled entry for it

### Other items (8)

- **R1-1** · nit · low · confirmed · `README.md:111` · Known limits does not say an uncounted mitigation commit goes unreviewed
- **R1-3** · nit · low · confirmed · `skills/redline/SKILL.md:184` · Stray space before a comma in the plan dial's field list
- **R1-4** · nit · low · confirmed · `templates/shape-spec-unattended.md:75` · The unattended section's return example omits the now-required `files`
- **R1-5** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:783` · New module-level `filled(item)` is shadowed by a local `filled(s)`
- **R1-6** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:2937` · The deferred outcome's mitigation fallbacks can no longer run
- **R1-7** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:3407` · A mitigation's words are hidden whenever the record says nothing ships, contrary to the comment and the docs
- **R1-8** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:3641` · draftsOf's default parameter names a const declared about 150 lines later
- **R1-12** · nit · low · confirmed · `workflows/redline-loop.js:4044` · The decided form of the "commit of its own" warning is pinned by no check and described by no doc

Each item has an inline comment with the detail or, where GitHub could not anchor it, sits under Not placed inline below. Redline replies in the item's thread, or in a PR comment that opens with its marker, with what it decided and why.

### Candidates set aside (1)

<details>
<summary>Refuted, collapsed or already tracked</summary>

- `workflows/redline-loop.js:3806` · isDeferral now treats any filled mitigation as the person's deferral, so a stray resolve entry worded `none` or `n/a` beside a call planned as a fix files a GitHub issue, and the fix's commit drops out of needCommits. Already tracked in #99, whose posted comment covers this; tests/loop-test.mjs:3088 (strayWorded) pins it as intended. · known: #99: a stray resolve entry beside a call answered with a fix is filed as the person's deferral. This pull request records the `none` case as a deliberate change (shape.md decision 14 and "Behaviour that changes on purpose"), pins it as intended in tests/loop-test.mjs:3088 (strayWorded), and drafts a comment on #99 about the commit demand it no longer makes.

</details>

comments.body:
**R1-1** · nit · low · confirmed

**Known limits does not say an uncounted mitigation commit goes unreviewed**

A deferral's mitigation commit is counted only if it is the finding's own (`ownCommit`, workflows/redline-loop.js:596-598): its subject opens `redline: <id>` or the implementer reported it for the finding. Otherwise `outcomesFor` zeroes it (2936-2938) and `fixed` leaves the finding out (4119). If nothing else in the round is fixed or bought, the run goes straight to the handoff. No final nit pass runs and no later round reads that code. Traced: a planned nit deferral (shaper files `['app/x.php']`) whose only commit is `redline: add a guard for R1-1 (#114)`, not reported for the finding. On this branch the reply is `deferred to #301.`, `fixed` is empty, `bought` is false, the run hands off and the planned-and-unbuilt warning fires. On main, `hasMitigation` was true, so the reply was `Mitigated in ...`, `fixed` held R1-1 and a final nit pass followed. README Known limits says such a commit `is not counted, so it is pushed with the round and named in no reply`. docs/running.md:125 says only that a counted commit `is reviewed like any fix`. Neither says the uncounted commit is read by no Redline pass. Conditions: the implementer departs from rule 3 of agents/redline-implementer.md twice (wrong subject and no report), and nothing else in the round earns a final nit pass or a re-review. If something does, the range the next pass reads runs from the previous head to the new one (4978), so it holds the commit anyway. shape.md records `not counted` as a change made on purpose; it does not mention the missing review. The repository's guard refuses `node` for the reviewer, so this was traced, not run. A harness that runs it against the branch and origin/main is at /tmp/redlinerepro/reviewer-r1-repro.mjs.

Proposed fix: Update README Known limits ("No commit is demanded of a deferral") and docs/running.md "Deferred items" (Whether a mitigation shipped) to add one clause: a commit that is not counted is read by no final nit pass or re-review unless something else in the round earns one.

**R1-2** · correctness · medium · confirmed

**The approver's file-list bounce reads the shaper's files for a finding the person decided**

Rule 1's new sentence makes it a bounce when a `defer` finding lists `files` with no task in `plan.md`, or has a task and lists none. The approver checks this against the findings planPrompt shows (workflows/redline-loop.js:2083). Those come from `effectiveDispositions()` (3838), which for a disposition override is the shaper's finding with only `disposition` replaced (3773-3776), so it keeps the shaper's `files`. The workflow itself never reads the shaper's list for a decided finding: it reads the resolve agent's tasks (`plannedFiles`, 3789-3791; `shaperPlanned` requires `!roundDecisions[id]`, 3785).

Two plan-dial paths meet the rule:
- A shaper fix (files listed) that the person changes to defer with nothing shipping. The resolve agent writes "no task when they name none" (2052), so the approver sees `"disposition": "defer"` with the fix's files and no task.
- A decline (`files: []`) overruled to defer with a mitigation that the resolve agent plans as a task. The approver sees a defer with a task and no files.

The rule calls both a bounce. A bounce runs a reshape (3857). The reshape prompt keeps a decision the person made "as it is" (2010), so a reshape that leaves that finding's files alone bounces again. After `maxPlanAdjustments` (2 by default, line 111) the round stops at approve (3853-3854).

Before this PR, rule 1 keyed on the mitigation ("A `defer` finding with an empty mitigation has no task, and that is no bounce"), so neither path bounced. Whether a given approver run bounces is that agent's call; its instructions tell it to.

Proposed fix: Show the approver the files the workflow reads. Either pass planPrompt each decided finding's resolve-task files (`plannedFiles`) in place of the shaper's `files`, or say in rule 1 that for a finding the prompt's decisions list, the resolve agent's task decides and the shaper's `files` are not read.

**R1-3** · nit · low · confirmed

**Stray space before a comma in the plan dial's field list**

This PR's edit to the plan-dial paragraph left `(the sentence Redline will post in the finding's thread) , \`decidedBy\``, with a space before the comma. The base branch read `... thread) and \`decidedBy\``.

Proposed fix: Write `(the sentence Redline will post in the finding's thread), \`decidedBy\``.

**R1-4** · nit · low · confirmed

**The unattended section's return example omits the now-required `files`**

The unattended section's return example (templates/shape-spec-unattended.md:71-76) shows no `files` on any finding, including the deferral R1-4 whose mitigation ships. This repository's copy at .claude/commands/agent-os/shape-spec.md:66 is the same. The sentence at line 97 that lists what every finding carries also leaves `files` out. Meanwhile:
- the shape schema now requires `files` (workflows/redline-loop.js:828);
- the example in agents/redline-shaper.md (39-44) lists it on every finding, R1-4 with `["app/Jobs/SyncOrders.php"]`;
- the shaper reads both texts.

shape.md ("Why the template is not touched") explains why the section's two prose sentences stay true, but does not mention the example. A shaper that copies the example returns a result the schema refuses and has to retry. When it fills `files`, the section it follows gives it no guidance. The cause is outside the diff: the template was not changed, and this PR's schema change made the example stale. A template change alters what a setup rerun writes, so the release standard makes it a minor bump with a setup rerun.

Proposed fix: Add `files` to every finding in the example in templates/shape-spec-unattended.md, matching agents/redline-shaper.md, and to the sentence at line 97, with the template marker and minor bump the release standard asks for. Otherwise, record in the spec why the example stays as it is.

The cause is in code this pull request did not change.

**R1-5** · nit · low · confirmed

**New module-level `filled(item)` is shadowed by a local `filled(s)`**

The new module-level `filled(item)` (783) takes a deferred entry and reads `item.mitigation`. The coverage parser declares its own `const filled = (s) => typeof s === 'string' && s.trim() !== ''` (1717-1718), which takes a string and shadows the module-level one inside that block. Neither block calls the other's helper today. An edit near 1717 that means the entry helper would get the string one, and `filled(entry)` would return false for every entry.

Proposed fix: Rename the module-level helper, for example `mitigationFilled`, at its one call in isDeferral (3806).

**R1-6** · nit · low · confirmed

**The deferred outcome's mitigation fallbacks can no longer run**

`shipsNothing` is now true whenever no commit of the finding's own landed (2936-2937), and `own` is a subset of `named`. So a deferred outcome either has commits (`shipped = named`, non-empty) or has `mitigation: ''` (2954). The fallback branches `outcome.mitigation ? ' Mitigation: ...'` in replyBody (1523) and `; mitigation: ...` in describeOutcome (2993) can never run. Deferred outcomes are only built at 2954 and copied with their commits at 3467. Those two branches are the only readers of the outcome's `mitigation` field. Before this PR they ran for a deferral whose words read as a mitigation and that had no commit.

Proposed fix: Remove the two fallback branches (1523, 2993) and the deferred outcome's `mitigation` field (2954).

**R1-7** · nit · low · confirmed

**A mitigation's words are hidden whenever the record says nothing ships, contrary to the comment and the docs**

`draftView` sets `mitigation: ships ? d.item.mitigation : ''` (3407), and `deferredEntry` keeps the words only when the outcome has commits (3387). So the words are blanked exactly when the record says nothing ships.

The new comment at 777-779 says the opposite: "The words are shown, at a stop and in the result, beside what the record says". docs/running.md:125 says the same ("the words of the mitigation, which are only shown"), and shape.md decision 1 says "The words are kept for display." draftView's own comment (3404) and the skill (skills/redline/SKILL.md:217, `empty when nothing ships`) describe what the code does.

The effect shows when the shaper writes a mitigation and a plan task but lists no `files`, the case the second warning (4044) exists for. The first stop (3684-3686) runs before any plan approver and shows `ships: false`, `mitigation: ''`, `files: []`, so the person sees no sign that a mitigation was written. The build can still commit it, and it is posted as mitigated; the only notice is the warning in the run's result.

Proposed fix: Either show the words at the stop whatever `ships` says, with the skill saying how to present `ships: false` beside written words, or correct the comment at 777-779 and docs/running.md:125 to say the words are shown only beside a mitigation that ships.

**R1-8** · nit · low · confirmed

**draftsOf's default parameter names a const declared about 150 lines later**

draftsOf's default `filesOf = plannedFiles` (3641) names a `const` declared at 3789. A default parameter is evaluated when the function is called, so any call without a second argument that runs before line 3789 throws `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'plannedFiles' before initialization`. Nothing does that today:
- the only early call, `shaperDrafts` (3653), passes `shaperFiles`;
- the later calls (draftStop at 3814, then 4022) run after 3789;
- plan.md's As built records this ordering.

The hazard is a future stop added before 3789, or a reorder. `plannedFiles` itself reads `roundDecisions` (3693) and `resolvedTasks` (3703), so moving its declaration up would not remove the ordering constraint.

Proposed fix: Drop the default and pass the files reader at every call: `draftsOf(list, shaperFiles)` at 3653, `draftsOf(list, plannedFiles)` at 3814 and 4022.

**R1-9** · correctness · low · confirmed

**A draft's version ignores the `ships` and `files` the stop now shows, so an answered draft is not raised again when they change**

A draft's version only counts changes to the issue text (3641-3646). issueDraft (1318-1330) holds the title, found, file and line, why and fullFix, and an answer covers every version up to the one it named (`draftAnswered`, 219). The stop now also shows `ships` and `files` (3405-3407): from the shaper's list at the first stop (3653), and from `plannedFiles` after the round's decisions. A reshape that changes a deferral's `files` but not its draft leaves the version unchanged, so `draftStop` after the reshape (3882) raises nothing. A person who answered Go ahead on `ships: false` is never shown that a mitigation now ships, and the build commits it with the reply `Mitigated in ...`.

The new approver rule (agents/redline-plan-approver.md:16) bounces exactly this mismatch (a deferral with a task in plan.md and no `files`), and a reshape that fixes the list is the expected outcome.

Traced on the guided dial:
1. The shaper defers R1-1 with a plan task, mitigation words and `files: []`.
2. The first stop shows `ships: false` and `mitigation: ''`.
3. The relaunch answers Go ahead for version 1.
4. The approver bounces, and the reshape lists `['app/x.php']`.
5. The draft text is unchanged, so version 1 still counts as answered.
6. The implementer commits `redline: R1-1 ...`, the outcome has its own commit, and it is posted as mitigated with no warning.

The version never covered the mitigation's words either, so a reshape that rewrote the words had the same gap on main. What this PR adds is `ships`/`files` on the stop and the bounce that changes them. Conditions: a shaper that lists no files for a planned mitigation (or lists files for none), a dial that raises drafts, and a reshape that corrects the list. Traced, not run; the harness is at /tmp/redlinerepro/reviewer-r1-repro.mjs (c5c6).

Proposed fix: Count the version over what the stop shows: include `ships`, the files and the mitigation words in the text compared at 3644, or keep a second fingerprint of them beside `text` and bump the version when it changes. Add a loop check: answer version 1 at a stop that shows `ships: false`, bounce, have the reshape list files, and expect a second stop.

**R1-10** · correctness · medium · confirmed

**deferralIds counts a decided call that a reshape re-sorted to defer, so its planned fix is no longer demanded**

`deferralIds` joins `finalDispositions.filter(defer)` to `deferred.filter(isDeferral)` (3949). The candidate reads the second list as already held in the first. It is not, and the difference is a lost commit demand.

How it happens:
- A judgment call's decision carries no `disposition` (autopilotDecision, 1364-1371; a person's answer to a call likewise).
- So `effectiveDispositions` gives such a finding whatever disposition a reshape returned (3773-3776).
- Suppose a reshape after a bounce sorts a decided call's finding as `defer` (the #97 R1-10 case; scenario strayReshape at tests/loop-test.mjs:3093).
- isDeferral says it is not a deferral (3804-3806). The reshape's entry is dropped as restated (3874-3879), so `resolveDeferred` never holds it.
- But `finalDispositions` says defer, so `deferralIds` holds it, and the resolve task that the person's answer planned is dropped from `needCommits` (3953).

Traced with strayReshape's scenario and no commit (`commitIds [[], []]`). On this branch the check passes with no repair and no warning: the finding is not in `roundDeferrals` (4022), so neither warning at 4036-4045 fires. The reply is `Redline round 1: Fix it now. No code change. · decided by: @author`. On main, the resolve-task clause demanded the task's commit (removed line `.concat(resolvedTasks.filter((task) => task.files.length && task.finding && !accepted.has(task.finding) && !record.forced[task.finding]).map((task) => task.finding))`, which had no deferral exclusion), and the round stopped at the check after its repair.

The candidate's other point holds: `deferred.filter(isDeferral)` is computed three times (3949, 4022, 4030), and each isDeferral call rebuilds `effectiveDispositions()`.

Conditions: a reshape that re-sorts a decided call to defer, and an implementer that skips that call's task. Traced, not run, since the guard refuses `node` to the reviewer; the harness at /tmp/redlinerepro/reviewer-r1-repro.mjs (c11) runs both branches.

Proposed fix: Build `deferralIds` from `deferred.filter(isDeferral)` alone. Compute it once after the build (`const roundDeferred = deferred.filter(isDeferral)`) and reuse it at 4022 and 4030. Add a loop check: strayReshape with `commitIds [[], []]` stops at the check with `no commit names R1-1`.

**R1-11** · correctness · medium · confirmed

**A person's override to fix is no longer demanded when the resolve agent returns a filled entry for it**

`needCommits` now leaves out every id in `deferralIds` (3949-3953). For a disposition override to `fix` (plan dial, decision `{disposition: 'fix'}`), isDeferral still returns true when the resolve agent's entry for the finding has a filled mitigation, even though the decision names `fix`. The test is `decision.disposition === 'defer' || (resolveDeferred.has(d.id) && (filled(d) || ...))` (3804-3806).

Traced: the shaper defers R1-1, the person overrides it to fix, and the resolve agent plans the fix's task but also returns `{mitigation: 'a guard', ...draft}`. The build leaves the fix out.
- `awayFromDefer` drops the shaper's entry (3727) and the resolve agent's entry is added (3766-3769).
- isDeferral is true, so `deferralIds` is {R1-1}, `needCommits` is empty, and the check passes with no repair.
- The draft is filed as #301 (4025-4028), and the outcome is decided with no commits (2948).
- The reply is `Redline round 1: Fix it in full. No code change. Deferred to #301. · decided by: @author`.
- The warning `round 1: R1-1 planned a mitigation in app/x.php and no commit of its own landed; posted as shipping nothing` fires, where app/x.php is the fix's task (`plannedFiles` reads `resolvedTasks`, 3789-3790).

On main the same entry was already read as a deferral (`hasMitigation`), but `needCommits` demanded the fix by its final disposition (removed line `.filter((f) => f.disposition === 'fix' || (f.disposition === 'defer' && mitigated(f.id)))`), so the round stopped at the check after its repair. On the guided and plan dials the person sees the stray draft at the stop after the resolve (`draftStop`, 3813-3828) and can drop it, but no answer there restores the demand. A bounce would drop the stray entry (`awayFromDefer` at 3879), so this needs a plan approved first time.

#99 tracks a stray entry beside a judgment call answered with a fix, and the comment this PR drafted for #99 (shape.md, "For you to add to #99") says a fix read as a deferral through a stray filled entry is no longer demanded. #99 does not cover the override case, and an override needs none of the new resolve-agent field #99 proposes: the decision already carries `disposition: 'fix'`, which isDeferral only reads when it is `defer`.

Conditions: the resolve agent returns a filled entry with a full draft for an override to fix. The override block of the resolve prompt (2052) does not forbid this; the "only when its decision defers" sentence (2046) covers calls only. Traced, not run; the harness is at /tmp/redlinerepro/reviewer-r1-repro.mjs (c1).

Proposed fix: In isDeferral, return false for a decision whose `disposition` is set and is not `defer` (an explicit override), before reading the entry. Alternatively, keep `needCommits` demanding every final `fix` and every resolve task of a decision whose disposition is `fix`. Add a loop check: the plan-dial override to fix with a stray `{mitigation: 'a guard'}` entry and no commit stops at the check with `no commit names R1-1` and files nothing.

**R1-12** · nit · low · confirmed

**The decided form of the "commit of its own" warning is pinned by no check and described by no doc**

The second warning has two texts (4044):
- for a finding the person or autopilot decided: `the resolve agent planned no task with files for it; posted with its decision`;
- otherwise: `the shaper listed no files for its task; posted as its mitigation`.

tests/loop-test.mjs pins only the shaper's text (2907). A search of tests/, docs/, README.md and skills/ finds the decided text nowhere, and docs/running.md:125 and the PR description list only the shaper's. A change to the decided branch stays green, and a person reading the run's result meets a warning the docs do not describe.

Proposed fix: Add a loop check: a call answered "Mitigate" whose resolve agent plans no task with files (`acceptedCalls`) and whose commit is the finding's own (`commitIds [['R1-1']]`), expecting the decided text. Name that text in docs/running.md, "Deferred items", Whether a mitigation shipped.
